newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET FLUSH, RATES DEPRESSED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET FLUSH, RATES DEPRESSED.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term money rates were quoted easier in Tuesday's liquid market, dealers said.
"It looks like the rates are softening a bit. With the (central Reserve Bank) rediscount rate at 23.5 percent, they won't want to see other rates go above that," one dealer said.
Market players however feel the rates should be going higher, given a rise in inflation to 22.4 percent in the year to April from 19.9 percent.

On Tuesday morning the central bank, forecasting a surplus of Z$1 billion from maturities, auctioned Z$235 million worth of 60-day treasury bills with an average yield of 23.09 percent, rejecting all bids that came in above the rediscount rate.
Another auction for Z$600 million worth of 36-day treasury bills was scheduled for later in the day.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were trading at 24 and 23 percent (buying and selling respectively), from 25.5 and 23.75 percent while call money shed two percentage points to 20 percent.
Bank acceptance bills were being bought at 23.5 percent from 24.5 percent and sold unchanged at 22 percent.
